fixes: P1 Palette: the board reads as a saturated Catan-style board game, not the game's muted wool. Measured in OKLab on the same board region of f1782 and the menu frame: the green fields have chroma 0.122 vs the menu's 0.074 (about 65% more) and lightness 0.56 vs 0.49. The orange hill hexes are candy orange where the menu's equivalent hex is a dusty terracotta-rose, and the wheat is lemon. Re-dye the satin to the game's sampled medians (target green C about 0.07-0.08, L about 0.49), give each hex a +/-3-5% dye-lot variation in hue and value, and grade both R25 and Eevee to the same targets. Without this, the hand-off to the menu cannot read as one image.

P1 Lighting and focal point: every frame is lit evenly, like a product shot. There is no pool, no falloff and no chiaroscuro, so nothing leads the eye and the stitch relief flattens out at full frame. The storyboard's act V light is in scope even without the desk: warm 3200 K pools at about 20 deg elevation and key:fill 4:1. Put Grandbois in the brightest pool, let the sea and the frame corners drop 1-1.5 stops, and keep it raking so the coupons and couching cast real micro-shadows. Today the bottom 40% of f1760 is flat, repetitive blue with no value structure.

P1 Clip-art icon repetition: every hill hex has the same lemon-yellow half-disc mounds, every wheat hex the same four tilted green rectangles, and every forest hex the same pine plus log pair. Sea wave ticks are scattered evenly per hex like wallpaper. This is the clearest sign of a procedural, AI-board-game look. Vary count, scale, rotation, placement and colour lot per hex, and follow the game's own tile layouts (3D crop rows, varied mounds). Replace the yellow discs with tonal laid-and-couched mounds with stem outlines. Cluster wave marks near the coasts and vary their size.

P1 Footprint ghosts: the stitched-elevation footprints left behind are darker than the satin around them. Grandbois leaves a dark green, two-spired castle silhouette across two hexes behind an octagonal plan-view model. Every pine and figure group gets a dark blob twin, and a dark-blue castle ghost sits in the sea at Sablon and Hautecouronne. They read as wrong-direction shadows or stains and are the main source of mud. Either do what S21 specifies (the stitched elevation becomes the front face of the 3D piece), or make the footprint the piece's own base outline in pale padding felt with needle holes, at a value lighter than the satin.

P1 Figure cards: they read as cardboard standees or stickers. The sprite art is soft (upsampled), has a cream die-cut border, and its cel outlines and smooth shading clash with the embroidery. Re-embroider the cards through R25 at 6 px/mm (split or satin strands with fuzz, a couched outline, appliqué thickness and wool sheen), or at least render them at native resolution with a stitch normal and height map and no cream rim.

P2 3D pieces: they look like plastic. The towns are grey-white low-poly with flat, untextured walls and glossy orange domes. Brumecourt and Vaugrise read as empty cream octagonal trays with a few houses, the quarry is untextured white boxes, and the pines are pale grey flat-bottomed cones that read as tents or umbrellas. Use a triplanar laid-and-couched normal at a visible stitch scale, a velvet or sheen lobe, a fuzz shell and per-face colour lots. Fill the town interiors. Make pines dark wool greens in clusters of 5-9 per forest hex with varied heights, matching the menu's forest density.

P2 Stitch-on: it reads as a digital wipe rather than a needle. Each hex first shows a flat vector-green padding fill, then confetti speckle along a sweep front. The reserved-linen icon holes are dilated blobs with a bevel or inner-shadow look, and the appliqué slips and towns pop in fully formed in one state. Fix: give the padding a visible felt or fibre texture, advance a few contiguous needle paths per hex rather than scattered dashes, tighten the reserved shapes to the icon outline, and couch slips and towns in over 3-4 states.

P2 Audio pacing: from f1708 to f1727 the frame-to-frame difference is at the grain floor, about 20 frames of dead air. The strongest accent in the window (the 'remembered' bass at f1726, strength 0.54) lands on a frame where the camera moves 0.02 deg and no piece has started. Keep gold-border tie-downs visibly stitching until f1719, and put a visible event on f1726: the coupon swell beginning, or the first piece snapping up on the beat.

P2 Climax pacing: all rises start by f1748 and visible motion has nearly died by about f1755, so the musical peak at f1760 (the loudest moment of the film) lands on a frame where only the faint +0.25 EV swell is still moving. Stagger the outer pieces (Sablon, Hautecouronne, the coast forests) to rise between f1744 and f1756 so the last tethers snap into the peak, and settle on f1760.

P3 River and sea: the river is a thin cyan vector-like stroke. Make it a couched cord of 2-3 blues at the menu's width. Add low-frequency dye-lot and value variation to the denim sea so it is not a uniform field.

P3 Shadows and tethers: Hautecouronne and the coast trees throw long dark-blue streaks across the sea that read as smears. Shorten or soften them. The 410 tethers can hardly be seen at full frame, and at 1:1 they read as white sticks or spears. Either make them read as wool (thicker, the realm colour, a catchlight, a visible snap recoil) or stop listing them as a feature.

P3 Hand-off identity: f1782 does not read as the menu's board. It has no shield markers, no nameplates and sparse forests, and the hexes look like separate tiles. Implement the S24 plan: from f1756, blend the board albedo into the UI-free menu plate, masked where pieces are still settling. Add the stitched shield markers so the last frame matches the game.
praise: The R25 core is good. At 1:1 the padded satin coupons show believable strand direction and grain. The couched gold realm borders with tie-downs, the cream running-stitch seams over a groove, and the laid-and-couched denim sea read as real needlework. The iron-gall underdrawing on bare linen ahead of the wave is tasteful and in period. The R25-to-Eevee swap is invisible. The crane is a single, motivated, smoothly eased move that lands exactly on the decoded menu camera, with no random moves. There is no particle spam and there are no glints, so the restraint is right. The layout registers with the menu's towns and coastline. This is a solid technical spine. What holds it back from the AAA bar is taste: the palette, the lighting, repeated clip-art icons, and 3D or card pieces that read as plastic and stickers.
